section_1_paragraph.name: section_1_paragraph
section_1_paragraph.default: 'Your relationship with money isn''t about maths. It''s about the patterns you learnt long before you had a salary. The eight money types, developed by Deborah Price of the Money Coaching Institute, give those patterns names. Most people carry three or four, with one or two in charge, and they shift as life does.'

section_1_paragraph_2.name: section_1_paragraph_2
section_1_paragraph_2.default: 'Below, each type as I see it in the coaching room. Read them, notice which ones sting, then take the quiz.'

section_2_paragraph.name: section_2_paragraph
section_2_paragraph.default: 'Money feels big, confusing and slightly frightening, so the Innocent looks away and hopes it sorts itself out. Bills stay unopened, statements unread. They''d much rather someone they trust handled it. Underneath is not laziness but anxiety: looking means finding out.'

section_2_text_3.name: section_2_text_3
section_2_text_3.default: 'In the coaching room: "I know I should check. I just… don''t."'

section_2_paragraph_2.name: section_2_paragraph_2
section_2_paragraph_2.default: 'Money happens *to* the Victim. The economy, the landlord, the ex, the boss: there''s always someone or something to blame, and often a real wound behind it. The pattern is waiting to be rescued rather than acting, which keeps the story true.'

section_2_text_6.name: section_2_text_6
section_2_text_6.default: 'In the coaching room: "What''s the point, it never works out for people like me."'

section_2_paragraph_3.name: section_2_paragraph_3
section_2_paragraph_3.default: 'Confident, disciplined, goal-driven. The Warrior sets a target, makes a plan, and uses both logic and gut to get there. This is the type most of us want more of. Its shadow is impatience with people who don''t think the same way, including partners.'

section_2_text_9.name: section_2_text_9
section_2_text_9.default: 'In the coaching room: "Just tell me the numbers and I''ll do it."'

section_2_paragraph_4.name: section_2_paragraph_4
section_2_paragraph_4.default: 'Generous to a fault. The Martyr pays for everyone, lends to anyone, and puts their own future last. Often there''s a quiet expectation that it will be repaid, in money or gratitude, and quiet resentment when it isn''t. Very common among parents and eldest siblings.'

section_2_text_12.name: section_2_text_12
section_2_text_12.default: 'In the coaching room: "I can''t say no to my family."'

section_2_paragraph_5.name: section_2_paragraph_5
section_2_paragraph_5.default: 'The Fool loves the thrill: the splurge, the hot tip, the crypto at 2am. Optimistic and lucky, money comes easily and leaves just as fast, because the pull of now beats the plan for later. Fun at dinner, dangerous in a bull market.'

section_2_text_15.name: section_2_text_15
section_2_text_15.default: 'In the coaching room: "I''ll make it back next month."'

section_2_paragraph_6.name: section_2_paragraph_6
section_2_paragraph_6.default: 'The Creator wants freedom, meaning and time, and suspects money is a bit grubby. So they under-charge, avoid the business side, and quietly block the wealth that would actually buy the freedom they want. The work is making peace with being paid well for good work.'

section_2_text_18.name: section_2_text_18
section_2_text_18.default: 'In the coaching room: "I didn''t get into this for the money."'

section_2_paragraph_7.name: section_2_paragraph_7
section_2_paragraph_7.default: 'A Warrior who went too far. The Tyrant uses money to control: the partner, the children, the staff. Every euro is tracked, every purchase questioned. It looks like strength, but it''s fear of losing control, and it costs relationships long before it costs money.'

section_2_text_21.name: section_2_text_21
section_2_text_21.default: 'In the coaching room: usually it''s the partner who books the session.'

section_2_paragraph_8.name: section_2_paragraph_8
section_2_paragraph_8.default: 'The Magician knows their money story, where the patterns came from, and chooses differently. Decisions line up with values. Money is a tool, not a threat. There''s security without obsession, generosity without martyrdom, ambition without tyranny. Nobody is born one. Everyone can become one.'

section_2_text_24.name: section_2_text_24
section_2_text_24.default: 'In the coaching room: this is where we''re heading.'

hero_paragraph.name: hero_paragraph
hero_paragraph.default: 'I brought money coaching to Malta in January 2023, when nobody here had heard of it. Since then I''ve coached hundreds of Maltese and European professionals who earn well but feel stuck: the ones who never learnt how money works and were told not to ask.'

story_paragraph.name: story_paragraph
story_paragraph.default: 'In my 20s, I thought strict money management and saving every cent was the key to financial success. I tracked everything down to the smallest detail and became obsessed with staying on top of my finances.'

story_paragraph_2.name: story_paragraph_2
story_paragraph_2.default: 'Then, in March 2019, I had two unexpected seizures while asleep. That experience forced me to reflect on how I was living. Financial wellbeing is far more than managing your cash flow: it''s about balancing the practical side of money with your emotional and psychological needs.'

story_quote.name: story_quote
story_quote.default: 'I don''t sell products and I don''t tell you what to buy. I help you understand your money story.'

story_paragraph_3.name: story_paragraph_3
story_paragraph_3.default: 'Today I balance ambition with joy, logic with emotion, and purpose with impact, and teach others to do the same: on stage, on screen, in the Times of Malta, and one-to-one.'

cta_heading.name: cta_heading
cta_heading.default: 'Ten minutes. No pitch. Just a conversation.'

cta_paragraph.name: cta_paragraph
cta_paragraph.default: 'Tell me what''s going on with your money. I''ll tell you honestly whether coaching will help.'
